note: Curated notable/giant stars beyond the HYG catalog. RA/Dec are well known; distances and radii are uncertain literature estimates.

stars.name: Stephenson 2-18
stars.note: Often cited as the largest known star — but its distance and size are heavily disputed.

stars.name: UY Scuti
stars.note: Long held as a record-holder for radius; Gaia data suggest the distance is uncertain.

stars.name: VY Canis Majoris
stars.note: One of the largest and most luminous stars known, shedding huge amounts of mass.

stars.name: WOH G64
stars.note: A vast red supergiant in the Large Magellanic Cloud — another galaxy.

stars.name: Mu Cephei
stars.note: Herschel's 'Garnet Star', one of the reddest naked-eye stars.

stars.name: VV Cephei A
stars.note: Eclipsing binary; the supergiant is among the largest stars known.

stars.name: Betelgeuse
stars.note: Shoulder of Orion; a nearby supergiant expected to go supernova.

stars.name: Antares
stars.note: Heart of Scorpius; a red supergiant rivalling Betelgeuse.

stars.name: Pistol Star
stars.note: Near the galactic centre; one of the most luminous stars in the Milky Way.

stars.name: R136a1
stars.note: The most MASSIVE known star (~196 M☉) — massive, not largest. In the LMC.

stars.name: Deneb
stars.note: Tail of Cygnus; intrinsically one of the most luminous nearby stars.

stars.name: Rigel
stars.note: Foot of Orion; a brilliant blue supergiant.
